newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BICC makes cash call for investments.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BICC makes cash call for investments.

text.p: British construction-to-cables group BICC Plc made a 170 million pound ($265 million) cash call to investors on Thursday, just one month after reporting a plunge into first half loss.
The company unveiled plans for a 2-for-11 rights issue of new shares at 270 pence per share to help fund investment opportunities worth more than 200 million pounds of
It also said it was likely to maintain the final dividend at 8.5 pence per share, taking the year's total to 12.5 pence.
"The time is right to focus on the future development of the business and significantly accelerate the pace of its investment to facilitate faster growth," chairman Viscount Weir said.
The group plans investment of around 140 million pounds in optical fibres, Brand-Rex data communications cables and high voltage cabling.
An extra 40 million is earmarked for the Asia-Pacific region and 35 million for equity investment in infrastructure projects which require private finance both in Britain and abroad.
Chief executive Alan Jones said investment was needed and, with gearing levels at around 80 percent, a cash call was considered the best option.
"I've been under pressure from our managing directors to make some investments," he said.
The money will be focused in the higher-margin products on the cable side of the business, adding extra capacity in key regions.
Jones said the investment would make the group's base "much more sound" and better able to withstand fierce pricing pressures and competition in the mass cable market.

BICC has undertaken a strategic shake-up for the past year in an effort to make itself more dynamic. In August it reported a half-year loss of two million pounds, skidding from a 60 million profit last year due to restructuring costs.
Analysts expressed concern then that as national utility and telecom companies were privatised, cosy relationships with cable suppliers would end.
They felt the tough pricing climate could continue for up to two years, leading players like BICC to concentrate on higher margin products.
BICC shares fell 2.5 pence after the news to 314 pence by 1410 GMT. ($1=.6412 Pound)
